turns.t: Oh, I'm so sorry I'm late, doctor. The bus, it just... and then I couldn't find the right room.
Don't give it another thought. You're here now. And this is your mother?
Yes, I'm Pauline. I hope it's all right that I came in with her. She was nervous.
Of course. Alice, it's your appointment, so you tell me what's brought you in, and your mum can add things if you'd like.
Well, it's... I've missed my period. And it's been, um, about ten days now.
I see. Is that unusual for you? Are your periods normally regular?
Usually. Like clockwork, mostly. That's why I... well, I got a bit worried.
That's completely understandable. Have you had any pain in your tummy?
No. No pain.
Any bleeding or spotting between periods, or at all in the last while?
No, not that I've... no.
Good. And how are your bowels and digestion generally?
Fine, I think. Yes. Fine.
Thank you. Now I'd like to ask about medicines. Do you take anything regularly?
Just the one. A little white tablet, um, every morning. I can't remember what it's called.
Do you know what it's for, or what the box says?
I... it's from the chemist, and it's in a... I don't have the box.
It's a small white one, love, with a line across it. I can't say the name either. We'll bring the box next time.
That's fine. We'll check with the pharmacy. Now, one more thing I always ask. Have you any allergies, to medicines especially?
Um. Yes. Penicillin.
Penicillin. And what happens when you take it?
I come out in hives. All over. It was when I was, um... quite small.
She was about six. Her whole back was covered. We've told every doctor since.
That's very useful, thank you both. I'll make sure it's clearly recorded, so nobody prescribes it by mistake.
Does it matter for... for today?
It matters for any prescription, whatever the visit is about. It's about keeping you safe. Now, let me check your blood pressure and pulse.
Blood pressure 118 over 74, pulse 80. Both perfectly healthy.
That's good, isn't it?
It's reassuring. Can you lie back on the couch for me? I'm going to feel your tummy, very gently.
Is this okay?
That's fine. Your abdomen feels soft all over.
Oh. Good.
And there's no tenderness anywhere when I press. Does it hurt at all?
No. It's just a bit ticklish.
Right, you can sit up. Let me explain my thinking, because I know you're worried.
Please.
A late period has many everyday causes. Changes in routine, stress, how much you've been eating, travel. It's very common.
She has had a lot on her plate lately.
Mum, don't.
It's all right, Alice. That's helpful to know, and it's something we can talk about calmly.
I just... I wanted to know it's nothing awful.
I hear you. There is nothing in what I've seen or heard today that frightens me. We'll see what the next days bring.
Okay. Thank you. I feel a little calmer.
Good. And Pauline, do bring the tablet box, and mind that penicillin note stays on her record.
We will. Thank you, doctor.

physical_examination.finding: Your abdomen feels soft all over

clinical_uncertainties.description: Patient cannot name her daily tablet, describes it as a little white tablet.
